title: feat(parser): inventory contracttype and contracterror types
problem: Structs and enums annotated with `#[contracttype]`/`#[contracterror]` define the contract's serialized interface but are not captured in the inventory.
why: Several planned detectors need to know the contract's data types and error variants.
scope: Capture annotated structs/enums with their name, kind, attributes, and span.
Record enum variant names for error types.
guidance: Extend `walk_items`; keep this separate from function facts.
acceptance: Tests cover struct and enum forms

title: feat(parser): record trait implementations on impl blocks
problem: `impl Trait for Type` blocks lose their trait path, so interface implementations cannot be distinguished from inherent impls.
why: Trait awareness supports interface and cross-module analysis.
scope: Store the optional trait path on impl summaries and functions.
acceptance: Tests cover inherent and trait impls

title: feat(parser): capture call argument positions and counts
problem: Detectors cannot tell which argument of a call is the address, amount, or key, limiting precision.
why: Argument awareness materially reduces false positives for token and storage rules.
scope: Extend `CallFact` with the number of arguments and the rendered text of each argument.
tests: Unit tests for method and function calls
security: Rendering arguments must not include unbounded source; truncate safely.

title: feat(parser): record string literal origin and symbol constructors
problem: String facts do not distinguish `symbol_short!(...)`, `Symbol::new(...)`, and ordinary literals, so key-related detectors cannot reason about key types.
why: Distinguishing key construction is necessary for collision and length detectors.
scope: Annotate string facts with the enclosing macro or constructor, if any.
guidance: Track the nearest enclosing macro while visiting.

title: feat(parser): inventory macro_rules definitions and invocations
problem: Macros can hide calls, authorization, and storage access, so detectors may miss real code.
why: Knowing where macros are defined and used lets the scanner explain coverage gaps.
scope: Record `macro_rules!` definitions and macro invocation names per file.
guidance: Collect `ItemMacro` and `Macro` nodes; do not attempt expansion.
acceptance: Inventory lists macro definitions and uses

title: fix(parser): normalize BOM and CRLF while preserving span accuracy
problem: A UTF-8 BOM or CRLF line endings can shift or confuse reported columns, especially on Windows-authored sources.
why: Inaccurate spans undermine report trust and SARIF annotations on GitHub.
scope: Strip a leading BOM and normalize line endings before parsing, keeping line numbering intact.
guidance: Normalize only for parsing; never write back to the source.
acceptance: Spans are correct for BOM and CRLF inputs
tests: Unit tests with BOM and CRLF byte sequences

title: feat(parser): detect generated-code markers and support exclusion
problem: Generated sources produce findings users cannot act on, and there is no way to exclude them by convention.
why: Excluding generated code by a documented marker reduces noise without broad path globs.
scope: Recognize `// @generated` and `include!` and either skip or mark those files, with a config toggle.
guidance: Default to marking (not silently skipping) and report the exclusion count.
tests: Corpus fixture with a generated marker
security: Do not silently ignore files; report exclusions.

title: feat(parser): inventory const and static values
problem: Constant values (TTL bounds, admin keys, limits) are not captured, so metadata-based detectors cannot use them.
scope: Record `const`/`static` names, types, and rendered initializers.
guidance: Reuse the same rendering helpers as function return types.
acceptance: Tests cover const, static, and const fn
security: Do not evaluate expressions; record them as text.

title: feat(parser): distinguish pub(crate) and pub(super) visibility
problem: Visibility is reduced to `pub` or not, so `pub(crate)` functions are treated as exported entry points.
why: Over-approximating exports can cause false positives in entry-point detectors.
scope: Represent visibility as an enum (public, crate, super, self, inherited).
tests: Unit tests for each visibility form
security: Prevents over-reporting private helpers as public entry points.

title: feat(parser): add parse telemetry to scan statistics
problem: Stats report files analyzed but not how many parsed successfully, failed, or were skipped.
why: Parse telemetry makes coverage gaps visible instead of silent.
scope: Add parsed, failed, and skipped counts to `ScanStats` and JSON output.
guidance: Derive counts from `ParsedSource` state during engine assembly.
acceptance: Tests assert counts for a mixed fixture
